_about: PRO batch 44: era 4, The Veteran (34-37), set 2.

scenarios.title: The Contract Incentives
scenarios.text: Your new contract has strict performance requirements: a percentage to hit, a number of games, a weight to stay under. Miss any of them, and the next year disappears.

choices.label: Tape them inside your locker
choices.result: Every requirement, taped inside your locker door where you see it every day. You check them each morning, and you hit all three by December.

choices.label: Forget they exist
choices.result: Forgotten, on purpose, after one careful read of the contract. You kick freely all season, and the requirements mostly take care of themselves.

choices.label: Plan the season around them
choices.result: The whole season, planned around the requirements with the training staff. It's careful and completely unglamorous, and it works, quietly, all year.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Recognition
scenarios.text: Your hometown wants to honor your career with a banner on Main Street, a dinner, and a day off for the schools. The mayor has already ordered the banner.

choices.label: Go home for the day
choices.result: Home for the day, with the whole family. The banner is enormous, the dinner is long, and {parent} cries at the high school band.

choices.label: Ask for a scholarship instead
choices.result: A scholarship for a local kid instead of the dinner. The town loves the idea, and the first winner is a kicker.

choices.label: Ask them to wait until you retire
choices.result: After you retire, you ask the mayor kindly. She agrees and keeps the banner folded in a closet, waiting for you.

scenarios.title: The Former Coach's Return
scenarios.text: A coach from early in your career, the special teams coach who cut you in camp once, is back in the league with your division rival. He sends a message: 'Still kicking?'

choices.label: Reply with a joke
choices.result: 'Still kicking,' you reply, with a photo of your old cut letter. He laughs, and you have dinner when your teams play.

choices.label: Thank him
choices.result: Thanks, for cutting you, because it made you. He's surprised and moved, and says he's told that story for years.

choices.label: Let your kicks answer
choices.result: No reply at all. You let the kicks answer for you, twice a year, in his stadium, in front of his bench.

scenarios.title: The Veteran's Perspective
scenarios.text: Younger players ask, at a team dinner, what the league was like when you came in. Phones, rules, money: they want to know everything that was different.

choices.label: Tell the stories
choices.result: The stories, all of them: flip phones, two-a-days, a team plane with no wi-fi. They laugh at everything and remember all of it.

choices.label: Tell them what hasn't changed
choices.result: What hasn't changed: the fear, the work, the people who help you. The table goes quiet, in a good way.

choices.label: Turn the question around
choices.result: What will they tell rookies in fifteen years? They argue about it until dessert, loudly, and you just listen and smile.

scenarios.title: The Unexpected Release
scenarios.text: Your first week at a new club, after the old one let you go in the middle of a season. The new coach says they need you Sunday, and the playbook is three hundred pages.

choices.label: Learn the playbook by Saturday
choices.result: Three hundred pages, learned by Saturday night, with coffee and a highlighter. On Sunday you know it better than half the roster.

choices.label: Lean on the new holder
choices.result: The new holder, asked for help, generously gives it: an evening of walkthroughs in the hotel parking lot. You trust each other by Friday.

choices.label: Keep it simple
choices.result: The kicking plays only, and nothing else. Simple, clean, and enough for Sunday, and you learn the rest over the next month.

scenarios.title: The Record Watch
scenarios.text: You're close to a major career milestone, a number only a handful of kickers have ever reached, and the league's statistics people have started emailing your agent.

choices.label: Count every one
choices.result: Every kick, counted, every single week. It's fun and nerve-racking at the same time, and you let yourself want it out loud for once.

choices.label: Don't count at all
choices.result: No counting, no reading, no talking. When it happens, the snapper tells you, and you hug him for a long time.

choices.label: Share it with the people who got you here
choices.result: Every interview about it turns into thanks: {holder}, the snappers, the coaches. The milestone ends up feeling like it belongs to everyone.

scenarios.title: After Football, in the Family Firm
scenarios.text: Your family wants you in the family business after football: the hardware store {parent} built, three towns now, with a desk already set up with your name on it.

choices.label: Say yes for after
choices.result: Yes, for after football. {parent} cries on the phone, and you start learning the business on Tuesday mornings in the offseason.

choices.label: Invest, but don't work there
choices.result: Money to expand, but your own path after football. The family understands, mostly, and the store grows to four towns.

choices.label: Say you don't know yet
choices.result: Honestly, you don't know yet, you tell them. The desk stays right there, waiting, and {sibling} jokes at every holiday about taking it over.

scenarios.title: The Old Training Facility
scenarios.text: You visit the facility where your pro career started, now used by a minor-league team. The weight room is the same, the paint is new, and your old locker still has a dent you made.

choices.label: Talk to the young players there
choices.result: An hour with the minor-league kickers, who don't believe you started here. You tell them it's true, and that the dent is yours.

choices.label: Walk the field alone
choices.result: The old practice field, walked alone at sunset. You remember the kid who kicked here and how scared he was.

choices.label: Take a photo for {parent}
choices.result: A photo of the dented locker, sent to {parent}, who remembers the day you made it and calls to tell you the story.

scenarios.title: The Record Falls
scenarios.text: A young kicker breaks one of your records: the longest kick in club history, in his second season. The reporters are at your locker before he's out of the shower.

choices.label: Congratulate him publicly
choices.result: Congratulations, on camera and in person, with a hug at his locker. He says your record was the one he grew up chasing.

choices.label: Joke about it
choices.result: Records are made to be broken, you say, but not that quickly. The clip goes around, and he texts you a laughing face.

choices.label: Go after it again
choices.result: Practice, extra long kicks, after everyone leaves. You'll probably never get it back, but it's fun to try every afternoon.

scenarios.title: The Agent's Advice
scenarios.text: Your agent takes you to lunch and says, gently, that it's time to prepare for retirement. Not now, necessarily. But the plan should exist before the decision does.

choices.label: Make the plan with them
choices.result: A plan, made over three lunches: the announcement, the money, the next job. It's the most useful thing your agent has ever done.

choices.label: Take it home first
choices.result: The conversation, taken home to the kitchen table that night. Your family has thoughts, and they're kinder than you expected.

choices.label: Insist you're not done
choices.result: There's more kicking in you, you tell your agent, firmly, over dessert. You mean to prove it this season, and your agent quietly orders a second coffee.

scenarios.title: The Former Teammate's Offer
scenarios.text: A retired teammate offers you a job at his company when you're done: sales, real money, a good team, and an office with a window and no kicking net.

choices.label: Say yes, for later
choices.result: Yes, for later, with a handshake and a lunch every season until you're ready. It's comforting to know there's a door.

choices.label: Shadow him for a week
choices.result: Seven days of shadowing in the offseason, in a borrowed tie. You're surprisingly good at it, and surprisingly bored by Thursday afternoon.

choices.label: Say football is your future
choices.result: Football, still, after football, you tell him warmly: coaching, broadcasting, something on a field. He understands completely and wishes you luck.

scenarios.title: The Final Home Game Question
scenarios.text: Your family asks, over a long Sunday dinner, whether this could be your last season. Nobody's pushing. They just want to know whether to be at every home game.

choices.label: Tell them it might be
choices.result: It might be, you say honestly. They decide to come to every home game, just in case, and you love seeing them in the stands.

choices.label: Tell them it isn't
choices.result: Not the last, you say firmly. They nod, a little relieved and a little worried, and pass the potatoes around.

choices.label: Ask what they want
choices.result: What do they want? The kids want one more season; {love_interest} wants you healthy. You hold both answers carefully, all spring.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Press Conference Rumor
scenarios.text: Reporters keep asking whether you've decided to retire. Every press conference, every locker visit, every charity event, the same question, phrased a dozen different ways.

choices.label: Give one answer and repeat it
choices.result: One answer, every single time: 'When I know, you'll know.' They stop asking by October, bored, which was the whole plan.

choices.label: Joke your way through it
choices.result: A different joke every week. The reporters start looking forward to it, and the question turns into a running bit.

choices.label: Ask the club to stop the questions
choices.result: The club's media staff, asked to keep the question out of press conferences. They do, and the room gets calmer.
